results.title: A Flexible Hardware Testbed for CubeSat Power System Resilience Testing
results.abstract: CubeSat Electrical Power Systems (EPS) are critical to mission success, yet remain a common source of failure due to limited validation under realistic operating conditions. This work presents the design, implementation, and validation of a modular CubeSat EPS architecture aimed at improving flexibility, efficiency, and system-level resilience. Notably, the proposed system employs a distributed maximum power point tracking (MPPT) approach and decouples energy harvesting from storage and load regulation. A combined simulation and experimental methodology is developed to evaluate system performance. A behavioral simulation model is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink to analyze control strategies and system dynamics, while a physical testbed is constructed to emulate CubeSat operating conditions using programmable solar inputs, configurable loads, and distributed sensing. This integrated approach supports the development of a digital twin framework for system validation. Results demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves stable operation and effective power management under varying input and load conditions. The distributed MPPT approach improves performance under non-uniform illumination, while the decoupled architecture enhances control flexibility. Simulation results show strong agreement with steady-state experimental behavior, though limitations in transient modeling highlight the importance of hardware validation. This work establishes a practical framework for developing and validating CubeSat EPS designs, providing a foundation for future research in resilient and adaptable small-satellite power systems.
